title.rendered: Authority Over Sickness in His Name: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: He gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease. Given. Delegated. Handed over. The authority to heal has been placed in the hands of the sent ones by the King Himself.

content.rendered:
When He had called His twelve disciples to Him, He gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease. Given. Delegated. Handed over. The authority to heal has been placed in the hands of the sent ones by the King Himself.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, August 5, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And when He had called His twelve disciples to Him, He gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease.”
Matthew 10:1 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Matthew 10 records the moment Jesus commissioned the twelve and sent them out on their first mission trip. Before He gave them their assignment, He gave them equipment. The Greek word for the “power” Jesus gave them is exousia, delegated authority. He put in their hands the same authority He had been walking in throughout Galilee. Authority over unclean spirits. Authority to heal all kinds of sickness. Authority to heal all kinds of disease. Not some. All.

The Amplified Bible Classic Edition expands the picture: “And Jesus summoned to Him His twelve disciples and gave them power and authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out, and to cure all kinds of disease and all kinds of weakness and infirmity” (Matthew 10:1 AMPC). Weakness. Infirmity. Disease. Every category of physical breakdown covered.

The Passion Translation adds: “Jesus called his twelve disciples to him and imparted to them authority to cast out demons and to heal every sickness and every disease” (Matthew 10:1 TPT). Every sickness. Every disease. The scope of the delegated authority is total.

Some Bible teachers have argued that this authority was only for the twelve, and only for that first-century mission. Two problems with that view. First, in Luke 10:1-9, Jesus extended the same commission to the seventy-two. Second, in Mark 16:17-18, Jesus said signs would follow those who believe, and named laying hands on the sick as one of those signs. Third, throughout the book of Acts, the healing authority was exercised by believers who were not among the original twelve, including Stephen, Philip, and Ananias. The apostolic authority to heal was not restricted to the twelve. It has been extended to every believer walking in the name of Jesus.

The important pastoral note is that not every prayer for healing results in visible healing on the timeline the believer expects. Even Paul, who healed many, was left with a thorn in his flesh he prayed three times to be removed and heard the Lord say, “My grace is sufficient for you.” The believer walks in the delegated authority to pray in Jesus’ name, and trusts the Father to answer according to His good and sovereign wisdom. What we do not do is stay silent because we cannot control the outcome. We speak, we lay hands, we anoint with oil, we pray in faith, and we leave the results in the hands of the King who delegated the authority.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the truth this morning is practical. When you or someone in your family is sick, do not hesitate to pray in the name of Jesus. Lay hands. Anoint with oil per James 5:14-15. Ask the Lord to heal. Trust Him with the outcome. The authority to speak has been given to you. Use it in humble, expectant faith.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have delegated authority to me in the name of Jesus to pray for the sick. Every sickness has a name and Jesus is above it. Every disease has a name and Jesus is above it. I do not stay silent because I cannot control the outcome. I speak in the name of Jesus, I lay hands where You lead me, I anoint with oil where the Word directs, and I trust You with what You will do. My part is faith and obedience. Your part is the answer. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The authority to heal in the name of Jesus has been delegated to me. I speak in faith, I lay hands where He leads, and I trust Him with the outcome. Every sickness is under His name.
